newsitem.title: USA: Electric restructuring passes Vermont senate.
newsitem.headline: Electric restructuring passes Vermont senate.

text.p: The Vermont Senate gave preliminary approval today to a bill that radically changes the way the electric industry does business in Vermont.

Tomorrow, several amendments are expected to dominate the debate before final approval is considered but Democrats are confident they have the votes to keep the bill essentially the same as the one approved today.

One of the most controversial parts of this complex bill was passed by the Senate today. This provision calls for both utility owners and ratepayers to pay for what's known as "stranded costs," the leftover effects of costly deals struck by the utilities.
The most prominent of these problematic investments involves Hydro-Quebec, which provides roughly a fifth of Vermont's power.

Currently, Hydro-Quebec sells electricity to the state at almost twice that of other providers, or over $0.06 per kilowatt hour. Green Mountain Power and other utilities are locked into a twenty year deal with Hydro-Quebec.
Until now, ratepayers have borne 100 percent of the cost for these investments.
Tomorrow, an amendment will be debated which provides incentives for Vermont Yankee, the state's lone nuclear plant, to shutdown within two years. That amendment is also likely to pass.
